title: Book 4 — Melpomene, Chapter 25
paragraphs: So far, I say, the land is known. But concerning the region north of the bald-headed men, no one can speak with certainty, for lofty, impassable mountains divide it off, and no one passes over them. These bald-headed men say, however—though I do not believe it—that the mountains are inhabited by men with goats' feet; and that after one has passed beyond them, others are found who sleep through six months of the year. This I do not accept as true at all. The country east of the bald-headed men, however, is known with certainty, being inhabited by the Issedonians. But what lies beyond both the bald-headed men and the Issedonians, towards the north wind, is unknown, except so far as we know it from the accounts given by these peoples just mentioned.
